                                              ACoT-VLA: Action Chain-of-Thought for Vision-Language-Action Models

                                                                      Abstract                                                                    Sub-tasks          Actions

                                         Vision-Language-Action models have emerged as essential
                                                                                                               (a)                 Pre-trained VLM                Action Policy
                                         generalist robot policies for diverse manipulation tasks,
                                         conventionally relying on directly translating multimodal
                                         inputs into actions via Vision-Language Model embeddings.                   Instruction    Observation
                                         Recent advancements have introduced explicit intermediary                                                Goal-image         Actions
                                         reasoning—such as sub-task prediction (language) or goal
                                         image synthesis (vision)—to guide action generation. How-
                                         ever, these intermediate reasoning are often indirect and in-         (b)                  World Model                   Action Policy
                                         herently limited in their capacity to convey the full, granu-
                                         lar information required for precise action execution. In-                  Instruction    Observation
                                         stead, we posit that the most effective form of reasoning
                                                                                                                                              Reference Actions      Actions
                                         is one that deliberates directly in the action space. We
                                         introduce Action Chain-of-Thought (ACoT), a paradigm
                                         where the reasoning process itself is formulated as a struc-          (c)                 Pre-trained VLM                Action Policy
                                         tured sequence of coarse action intents that guide the fi-
                                         nal policy. In this paper, we propose ACoT-VLA, a novel                     Instruction    Observation
                                         architecture that materializes the ACoT paradigm. Specif-
                                                                                                               Figure 1. Chain-of-Thought in different space. (a) Language CoT
                                         ically, we introduce two complementary components: an
                                                                                                               paradigm predicts sub-tasks as intermediate reasoning. (b) Visual
                                         Explicit Action Reasoner (EAR) and Implicit Action Rea-               CoT paradigm synthesizes a goal image to provide guidance for
                                         soner (IAR). The former proposes coarse reference trajecto-           action policy. (c) Our proposed Action CoT directly operates in
                                         ries as explicit action-level reasoning steps, while the latter       action space and provides homogeneous action guidance.
                                         extracts latent action priors from internal representations of
                                         multimodal input, co-forming an ACoT that conditions the              Recent advancements seek to improve the mapping from
                                         downstream action head to enable grounded policy learn-               the input space to the action space by introducing the in-
                                         ing. Extensive experiments in real-world and simulation               termediate reasoning step by language generation, leading
                                         environments demonstrate the superiority of our proposed              to more generalized and precise action outputs [22, 55], as
                                         method. Code is available at: https://github.com/                     visualized in Fig. 1(a). A parallel thrust leverages world
                                         AgibotTech/ACoT-VLA.                                                  models [16, 51, 67] to simulate environmental dynamics, di-
                                                                                                               rectly enhancing the efficacy and goal-oriented nature of the
                                                                                                               generated action sequences [60, 64], as shown in Fig. 1(b).
                                         1. Introduction                                                          Despite the promising trajectory set by these paradigms,
                                                                                                               a critical challenge persists: existing generalist policies
                                         To overcome the generalization limits of task-specific robot
                                                                                                               think predominantly in the vision-language (input) space,
                                         policies [11, 48, 63], recent work has converged on Vision-
                                                                                                               often failing to adequately address the inherent disparity
                                         Language-Action (VLA) models [5, 24, 33, 41], which
                                                                                                               between these rich, semantic representations and the re-
                                         always leverage a pre-trained Vision-Language Model
                                                                                                               quirements of precise, low-level action execution (output).
                                         (VLM) [1, 2, 46] to encode visual and linguistic inputs into
                                                                                                               Specifically, the knowledge encoded within the VLM back-
                                         a latent representation that conditions an action decoder.
                                                                                                               bone of VLA models is derived from pre-training on web-

Figure 2. Architectural Overview of ACoT-VLA. The framework consists of three main components operating on features from a shared
VLM backbone. (a) The Explicit Action Reasoner (EAR) is a Transformer-based module that synthesizes a coarse reference trajectory,
providing explicit action-space guidance. (b) The Implicit Action Reasoner (IAR) employs a cross-attention mechanism with learnable
queries to extract latent action priors from the VLM’s internal representations. (c) The Action-Guided Prediction (AGP) head synergisti-
cally integrates both explicit and implicit guidances via cross-attention to condition the final denoising process, producing the executable
action sequence.

                                                                   14
E. LLM Usage Statement
In this paper, we employ Large Language Models (LLMs)
solely for minor linguistic refinement during the manuscript
preparation stage, such as correcting grammatical errors.
None of the technical content, implementation details, or
experimental results were generated by LLMs.
